standard_prerequisites: The category of topological A-algebras complete along I for a Noetherian ring A with ideal I (the displayed category in the source section), and the rig-smooth property over the pair (A, I)
The completed naive cotangent complex NL and its long exact sequence, as developed in the same chapter
The uniformity integers d and q of the associated graded Gr_I(B) from the local cohomology section cited in the proof
core_obligations: From the hypotheses deduce rig-smoothness of B over (A, I) and the divisibility data b' Delta = b, I^c B subset bB

Build the finite type A-algebra C adding variables z_i with relations z_i Delta' - a_i^c, compute the Jacobian determinant (Delta')^{t+1}, and bound the annihilator of Ext^1 of NL by a power of I independent of the truncation n
Transport the annihilation to the completion C^wedge and conclude C^wedge is rig-smooth over (A, I)

Construct the surjection psi_n mod I^n, lift it to a homomorphism phi : C^wedge to B congruent mod I^{n-(d+1)c_1}, prove surjectivity, and control Ker(phi)/Ker(phi)^2 by the rig-smooth exact sequence plus localization at b, where both H^0 terms are free of rank r-m
proof_roadmap: Reduce the hypotheses to rig-smoothness of B and the arithmetic of b, b', c, b_i
Choose truncations f'_i mod I^n, form C, compute its determinant (Delta')^{t+1} and the I-annihilation exponent c_1
Conclude C^wedge rig-smooth over (A, I) by base change of the Ext annihilation
Lift psi_n to phi using the uniformity bounds, then finish via the NL exact sequence and the rank computation after inverting b
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is an algebraization statement: an adic Noetherian algebra with an approximate presentation satisfying a divisorial Jacobian bound is the completion of a finite type A-algebra (source lines 1637-1760, label lemma-approximate-presentation-rig-smooth). The solver must engineer an auxiliary finite type algebra with an explicit Jacobian determinant, convert it into an I-annihilation bound independent of the truncation parameter, and then run a lift-plus-kernel-control argument whose final step is a rank computation after inverting b; none of this follows from a standard citation. Allowed background: the chapter's NL machinery, the rig-smooth criterion lemmas and the cited uniformity section, delivered as navigation pointers.
